speaker: Unknown
en: Security teams don't need another list of alerts.
zh: 安全团队不需要又一堆警报列表。

en: They need to know which vulnerabilities are actually reachable, exposed, and safe to fix.
zh: 他们需要知道哪些漏洞实际上是可达的、暴露的、并且可以安全修复的。

zh: 这就是 Blitzy 的 Hyperscale 修复（remediation）所做的。

zh: Blitzy 理解你的整个软件资产，然后在你的代码库中找出已知的和此前未被发现的漏洞。

speaker: Unknown
en: It traces each one through the execution paths, checks the dependencies, and validates the fix.
zh: 它追踪每一个漏洞的执行路径，检查依赖项，并验证修复。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your engineers approve the plan and Blitzy delivers batches of tested pull requests ready to review.
zh: 你的工程师批准计划，Blitzy 交付一批批经过测试、随时可供审查的 pull request。

speaker: Unknown
en: Less alert noise, faster remediation, and confidence that fixes are validated as safe before you review them.
zh: 更少的警报噪音，更快的修复，以及在审查之前就能确信修复已被验证是安全的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Visit Blitzy.com to see it in action.
zh: 访问 Blitzy.com 看看它的实际效果。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's B-L-I-T-Z-Y dot com.
zh: 那就是 B-L-I-T-Z-Y 点 com。

en: TikTok is known for getting you to buy things you never knew you wanted.
zh: TikTok 以让你买到你从不知道自己想要的东西而闻名。

speaker: Unknown
en: Online retailers would love that kind of impact, but they don't have TikTok's data.
zh: 在线零售商很想要这种影响力，但他们没有 TikTok 的数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they try to show the shopper what they're looking for and hope that sales will follow.
zh: 所以他们试图向购物者展示他们正在寻找的东西，并希望销售随之而来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Optimizing for what you can measure is not unique to e-commerce.
zh: 为你能衡量的东西做优化，并不是电商独有的。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI teams often settle twice.
zh: AI 团队常常妥协两次。

speaker: Unknown
en: They lean on signals that are easy to collect, like a click or a thumbs up, and they optimize for metrics that are easiest to evaluate, like relevance or benchmark accuracy.
zh: 他们依赖容易收集的信号，比如点击或点赞，并且他们针对最容易评估的指标做优化，比如相关性或基准测试准确率。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then they hope it all adds up to what they actually care about.
zh: 然后他们希望这一切加总起来就是他们真正关心的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're building a RAG system, a copilot, or an agent, you may be making the same bet.
zh: 如果你在构建 RAG 系统、copilot 或智能体，你可能正在做同样的赌注。

speaker: Unknown
en: Zoe Weil's answer, at least in retail, is to look between the clicks.
zh: Zoe Weil 的答案，至少在零售领域，是去看点击之间的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: The company she co-founded and leads, Sequin, is built on signals most systems ignore.
zh: 她共同创立并领导的 Sequin 公司，建立在大多数系统忽略的信号之上。

speaker: Unknown
en: How long a shopper hesitates, how fast they scroll, and how many times they go back and forth between two products before adding one to the cart.
zh: 购物者犹豫了多久，他们滚动的速度有多快，以及他们在把一个商品加入购物车之前，在两个商品之间来回比较了多少次。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it judges the results not by what people click, but by what they buy.
zh: 而且它评判结果不是看人们点了什么，而是看他们买了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I push back on two things, whether this is just age-old upsell and cross-sell with better data and where it starts to look like surveillance.
zh: 我在两件事上提出了质疑：这是否只是换汤不换药的追加销售和交叉销售（有了更好的数据），以及它何时开始看起来像监视。

speaker: Unknown
en: But she made a point about the playbook most teams follow that I hadn't heard put this bluntly.
zh: 但她关于大多数团队所遵循的打法（playbook）的观点，是我从未听人说得这么直白的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The biggest innovators in the space are social media companies, and they publish a lot in this, right?
zh: 这个领域最大的创新者是社交媒体公司，他们在这方面发表了很多成果，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: But they have a wealth of data that none of our customers have.
zh: 但他们拥有我们的任何客户都没有的海量数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you're a scientist at Wayfair,
zh: 所以如果你是 Wayfair 的一名科学家，

speaker: Unknown
en: Or a price line.
zh: 或者是 Price Line 的。

zh: 你会去读这些论文，然后你会尝试去实现它。

en: And you know what?
zh: 而你知道吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Oftentimes you're successful at implementing it, except guess what?
zh: 很多时候你成功地实现了它，只不过猜怎么着？

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't drive the same outcomes for you as it does for them because you don't have the data that they have.
zh: 它不会给你带来和他们一样的结果，因为你没有他们拥有的数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Seguin's big unlock is that we're finally able to get you that unlock without you having that data.
zh: 而 Sequin 的重大突破在于，我们终于能够让你在没有那些数据的情况下获得那个突破。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Sam Charrington, and this is the TwiML AI Podcast.
zh: 我是 Sam Charrington，这是 TwiML AI 播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: For over a decade, I've been exploring the ideas and innovations shaping the future of AI through conversations like this one that help you understand what's real, what's next, and what matters.
zh: 十多年来，我一直在通过像本期这样的对话，探索塑造 AI 未来的理念与创新，帮助你理解什么是真实的、什么是下一个、什么才是重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's jump in.
zh: 我们开始吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: So anything that you see on the internet is ranked, right?
zh: 你在互联网上看到的任何东西都是被排序的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Whether it's a pair of pants that you're looking for at a retailer, hotels that you're looking for for your next travel, content, media, even the ads you see online.
zh: 无论是你在零售商那里找的一条裤子，你为下次旅行找的酒店，内容、媒体，甚至你在网上看到的广告。

speaker: Unknown
en: are powered by an auction.
zh: 都是由竞价系统驱动的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And these seem maybe to most people to be unrelated, but every dollar of online spending consumption goes through a ranking model somewhere.
zh: 这些在大多数人看来也许互不相关，但线上消费的每一美元都经过某个地方的排序模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we power those ranking models for the world's largest consumer companies.
zh: 而我们为世界上最大的消费公司提供这些排序模型的支持。

speaker: Unknown
en: Walk me through kind of the highlights of what you all are doing, what makes your approach unique and, you know, with an eye towards or ear towards the kind of technical innovations.
zh: 带我了解一下你们都在做什么的要点，你们的方法有什么独特之处，并且，你知道的，带着对这类技术创新的关注去听。

speaker: Unknown
en: Unsurprisingly, when people think about ranking, they think about information retrieval.
zh: 不出意外，当人们想到排序时，他们会想到信息检索。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, I went to graduate school for information retrieval, which is literally the study of search systems, right?
zh: 事实上，我读研究生时学的就是信息检索，它字面上就是研究搜索系统的学科，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do I retrieve the most relevant items or documents for a given query, whether that's
zh: 如何为给定的查询检索出最相关的条目或文档，无论那是在

speaker: Unknown
en: In a search bar or some kind of relevance module somewhere out there.
zh: 搜索栏里，还是在外面某个地方的相关性模块里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And historically, and again, quite, I would say intuitively, the wisdom here has been that utility should be measured by whether or not I'm able to retrieve documents that are most semantically relevant to a user's query, right?
zh: 而从历史上看，再说一次，我会说相当符合直觉地，这里的共识一直是：效用应该以我是否能检索出与用户查询在语义上最相关的文档来衡量，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a very technical side of it.
zh: 这是它非常技术性的一面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that works incredibly well.
zh: 而这非常有效。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I would say, by and large,
zh: 我会说，大体上，

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe it's not a solved area of research, but there have been so many advances on it.
zh: 也许它还不是一个已被解决的研究领域，但已经有很多进展了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's been pretty remarkable.
zh: 这一直相当惊人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, the frontier labs have it, you know, pat down or down pat.
zh: 我的意思是，前沿实验室已经把它掌握得炉火纯青了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I forget what the idiom is, but they're pretty good at it.
zh: 我忘了那个习语是什么，但他们在这方面相当擅长。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not really on its own an interesting, I would say, area of research.
zh: 我想说，它本身其实并不是一个有趣的研究领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: However, in a commercial context, you know, modern recommender systems, if you think about TikTok, Instagram, and the like, they're not really recommending content anymore, and they're definitely not trying to help people find things.
zh: 然而，在商业语境下，你知道，现代推荐系统——如果你想想 TikTok、Instagram 之类——它们其实已经不再是在推荐内容了，它们也绝对不是在帮助人们发现东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Instead, they're bending the end user's will in subtle ways over time to make them want things that they otherwise wouldn't want, right?
zh: 相反，它们是在随着时间推移以微妙的方式扭曲终端用户的意愿，让他们想要那些原本不会想要的东西，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So that destination vacation,
zh: 比如那个度假目的地，

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, the latest fashion that you might not need, you know, whatever it is that you can think of that people end up just, you know, buying on Instagram or TikTok.
zh: 你知道的，你可能并不需要的最新时尚单品，你能想到的任何东西，人们最终就在 Instagram 或 TikTok 上买了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They do that not because Instagram and TikTok are, you know, really good at helping you find what you're looking for.
zh: 他们能做到这一点，并不是因为 Instagram 和 TikTok 真的很擅长帮你找到你在找的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, they're very, very good at influencing your behavior.
zh: 不，它们非常非常擅长影响你的行为。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason that they're able to do that is that billions of people use their apps and are frankly addicted to those apps.
zh: 而它们之所以能做到这一点，是因为有数十亿人在使用它们的应用，而且坦白说对这些应用上了瘾。

speaker: Unknown
en: They open their apps 10 to 21 times a day.
zh: 他们每天打开这些应用 10 到 21 次。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when billions of people do that, you have an insane amount of data on them.
zh: 而当数十亿人都这样做时，你就拥有了关于他们的海量得疯狂的数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you're able to create these incredibly immersive, I would even say addictive experiences that are hyper-personalized and dynamic.
zh: 于是你就能创造出这些极其沉浸式、我甚至可以说是令人上瘾的体验，既高度个性化又是动态的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in fact, the apps react in real time to the user's feedback, right?
zh: 而且事实上，这些应用会实时对用户的反馈做出反应，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So even, you know, you Sam, if you, what you see on the site or the app in the day, throughout the day will vary based on your interactions with the app.
zh: 所以即便是你，Sam，如果你——你在一天之中在网站或应用上看到的内容，会根据你与应用的互动而变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the truth is that consumer companies, regardless of how large they are, you know, regardless of how many customers they have, Wayfair is a good example.
zh: 但事实是，消费类公司无论规模多大，你知道，无论拥有多少客户——Wayfair 就是一个很好的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Priceline is another really good example.
zh: Priceline 是另一个非常好的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are very large companies that have incredibly large user bases, do tens of billions of dollars of online transactions.
zh: 这些都是非常大的公司，拥有极其庞大的用户群，进行着数百亿美元的在线交易。

speaker: Unknown
en: But again, people don't use Wayfair the same way that they use Instagram or TikTok.
zh: 但话说回来，人们使用 Wayfair 的方式和使用 Instagram 或 TikTok 是不一样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so regardless of how big you are as a consumer business, you are going to be data starved.
zh: 所以，无论你作为一家消费类业务规模有多大，你都会面临数据匮乏。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so in an environment where you don't have as much data on the user, where people are not addicted to your app,
zh: 于是在一个你对用户没有那么多数据、人们没有对你的应用上瘾的环境里，

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you influence their behavior in a moment of high intent to increase their basket size, increase their average order value, to increase their engagement on your site?
zh: 你如何在高意图的时刻影响他们的行为，来提高他们的购物篮规模、提高他们的平均订单价值、提高他们在你网站上的参与度？

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, these aren't like big changes.
zh: 再说一遍，这些并不是什么大的改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: So on Wafer, for example, if you're going to buy a $100 couch, it's not like Sequelink can come in and get you to buy a $500 couch and also a $1,000 coffee table.
zh: 比如在 Wafer 上，如果你要买一张 100 美元的沙发，并不是说 Sequelink 能进来让你买一张 500 美元的沙发，再外加一张 1000 美元的咖啡桌。

speaker: Unknown
en: The point is I can get people to buy $102, but I can do it consistently and at scale.
zh: 关键是，我能让人们多买 2 美元，但我可以持续地、大规模地做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you do that,
zh: 而当你做到这一点时，

speaker: Unknown
en: That translates to Forexing their target profit for the year in less than a month.
zh: 那就转化成了在不到一个月内达到 Forexing 他们全年的目标利润。

speaker: Unknown
en: Upsell, cross-sell, like we've been, you know, doing this from a data science perspective, pre-data science, you know, we've been doing this for a long, long time, trying to get people to buy more.
zh: 追加销售、交叉销售，就像我们——你知道，我们从数据科学的角度、前数据科学时代就已经在做这件事了，我们做这件事已经很久很久了，试图让人们买得更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's different about the approach?
zh: 这个方法有什么不同之处？

speaker: Unknown
en: The TLDR, as I was saying earlier, and in fact, for the entire history of this field of research, people have been trying, the wisdom has been, if I can make it easier for people to help to find things, then by extension, I can get them to convert better.
zh: 简单说，正如我之前所说，事实上，纵观这个研究领域整个的历史，人们一直在尝试——主流观点一直是：如果我能让人们更容易找到东西，那么推而广之，我就能让他们的转化更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: That has been the prevailing wisdom forever.
zh: 这一直是长期以来的主流观念。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every company that's ever existed in this domain has been trying to solve search and relevance from the perspective of search and relevance, make it easier for people to find things faster.
zh: 这个领域存在过的每一家公司，都在从搜索和相关性的角度来解决搜索和相关性问题——让人们更容易更快地找到东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is not what Sequin does at all.
zh: 而那完全不是 Sequin 所做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are not at all trying to help people find things.
zh: 我们完全不是在试图帮助人们找到东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're trying to influence their behavior in a moment of time when they have high intent.
zh: 我们是在试图在他们具有高意图的那个时刻影响他们的行为。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we do that?
zh: 我们怎么做到这一点？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we go about doing that?
zh: 我们是如何着手做到这一点的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Which is I think the meat of the matter.
zh: 我认为这才是问题的关键所在。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we started the company with a black box solution that was powered by what we call large event models.
zh: 所以我们创立公司时采用了一个黑盒解决方案，它由我们称之为大型事件模型的东西驱动。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can think of it as, first of all, it's not a large language model.
zh: 你可以这样理解：首先，它不是大语言模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: We actually don't use large language models anywhere.
zh: 我们实际上在任何地方都没有使用大语言模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not our business whatsoever.
zh: 那完全不是我们的业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we don't use generative AI either.
zh: 我们也不使用生成式 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in any case, so we started with large event models.
zh: 不管怎样，所以我们从大型事件模型开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the idea behind large event models is that the same way that large language models are able to generalize.
zh: 大型事件模型背后的理念是：就像大语言模型能够泛化

speaker: Unknown
en: to text, including text that they haven't seen before ever.
zh: 到文本，包括它们以前从未见过的文本一样，

speaker: Unknown
en: Large event models are able to generalize to human behavior and streams of events all in real time.
zh: 大型事件模型能够泛化到人类行为和事件流，而且全部是实时的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Creating something like that is incredibly difficult to do for a number of reasons.
zh: 创造这样的东西是极其困难的，原因有很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: One, you need to be able to create extremely ultra low latency systems that are able to keep track of data at a very, very fine grained level, right?
zh: 第一，你需要能够构建极其超低延迟的系统，这些系统能够以非常非常细的粒度跟踪数据，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm not only talking about clicks and conversions and the traditional good stuff, although we use that as well.
zh: 所以我谈的不仅仅是点击、转化和那些传统的好的指标，虽然我们也使用这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I'm talking about hovers, scrolls.
zh: 但我谈的是悬停、滚动。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm actually talking even deeper than that.
zh: 实际上我谈的甚至更深。

speaker: Unknown
en: The speed of a scroll, right?
zh: 滚动的速度，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: The dwell time on a hover.
zh: 悬停时的停留时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: How many times a user goes back and forth.
zh: 一个用户来回往复的次数。

speaker: Unknown
en: Creating systems that are able to digest data in, frankly, nanoseconds, transform this data also in nanoseconds, put it through a model, several layers of ranking models,
zh: 构建能够说实话在纳秒级消化数据的系统，同样在纳秒级转换这些数据，把它送入一个模型、好几层排序模型，

speaker: Unknown
en: in milliseconds and serve dynamic re-ranked items to a user as they're browsing a site all in under 50 milliseconds for thousands of requests per second is incredibly difficult to do.
zh: 在毫秒级完成，并在用户浏览网站时向其提供动态重排序的条目，全部在 50 毫秒以内、每秒数千个请求，这是极其难以做到的。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, we created what we refer to internally as sequence ranking clusters to be able to even make this feasible at all.
zh: 事实上，我们创建了内部称为序列排序集群的东西，才能让这件事勉强可行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there was a lot of work done there, not only from an algo perspective, but also from a data engineering perspective, feature engineering perspective, specifically for ranking and a ton of MLOps work and infrastructure work that was done.
zh: 所以那里做了大量工作，不仅是算法层面，还有数据工程层面、特征工程层面，特别是针对排序的，还有大量的 MLOps 工作和基础设施工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's hard because you need to do three things that are very, very difficult to do on their own.
zh: 这很难，因为你需要做三件单独来看就非常非常难的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to have high fidelity, leakage-free data pipelines, which is a really difficult problem on its own.
zh: 你需要有高保真的、无泄漏的数据管道，这本身就是一个非常难的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to have, obviously, models that are personalized to every user and continue to improve on those models.
zh: 你显然需要有针对每个用户个性化的模型，并且持续改进这些模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you need to be able to serve them fast enough such that rankings are able to react to live user feedback and signals.
zh: 然后你需要能够足够快地提供服务，使得排序能够对实时的用户反馈和信号做出反应。

speaker: Unknown
en: So building this system at all requires you to do these three things really, really, really, really well.
zh: 所以构建这样的系统本身就要求你把这三件事做得真的、真的、真的、真的非常好。
